One of the major concerns facing societies today is how to use energy from natural and non-renewable resources efficiently. What role do imported double-glazed glass production machines play in this regard?
Since the greatest energy losses occur in buildings, one of the most effective solutions is to use windows fitted with double-glazed glass.

settings.title: History of Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
Glass was already in common use among the Romans around 1,000 BC, while its widespread use dates back approximately 200 years.
The first patent for double-glazed glass was granted in 1865 to the owner of a glass shop in New York.
His studies demonstrated that double glazing could effectively maintain the temperature inside buildings.
Double- or multi-glazed glass consists of several parallel glass panes mounted opposite one another in an aluminium frame, with the space between them filled with an inert gas.

settings.title: Why Use Double-Glazed Glass?
settings.text:
As mentioned earlier, energy is lost through building windows, and it is estimated that around 40% of heat escapes this way.
Single-pane glass readily transfers heat between indoor and outdoor environments. As a result, building heating systems in cold seasons and cooling systems in warm seasons cannot operate efficiently.
Consequently, a significant amount of heating and cooling energy is wasted. One of the most effective ways to prevent this is to install double-glazed windows.
Air molecules can significantly reduce the transfer of heat and cold. This useful property is why special gases are used in double-glazed glass to create an insulating layer.
To explain, double-glazed glass consists of two panes, with the gap between them filled with argon gas.
This creates a sealed, two-layer glass barrier that acts as insulation and significantly reduces energy loss.
The benefits of installing double-glazed glass can be summarised as follows:
1. Reduces heat loss and, consequently, building energy costs
2. Provides sound insulation
3. Improves window security
4. Reduces condensation on the glass, meaning less fogging

settings.title: Double-Glazed Glass Production Process in the Factory
settings.text:
Now that you have useful, comprehensive information about double-glazed glass and its features, it is worth taking a brief look at the production line for these products.
First, glass sheets are placed on the rails of the automatic handling system. After the operator checks their dimensions and quantity, they are transferred to the cutting table.
The glass dimensions are then laid out using software and cut by the machine to minimise waste.
Next, the glass is transferred to the production line, where it is first treated with softened water and thoroughly washed in glass-washing machines.
The spacer bars between the two panes are then bent to the required dimensions and glass thickness using a dedicated bending machine. The inside of each spacer is filled with desiccant.
The two edges of the spacer are sealed with butyl using a butyl applicator, preparing the glass for assembly onto the frame.
After the glass is mounted on the frame, it is placed in a press while argon gas is injected into the cavity between the panes.
Finally, the finished double-glazed unit is filled with polysulfide sealant to provide secondary sealing.
